title: Mixing: Thrillington by Paul and Linda McCartney | 1971
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, Abbey Road
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Tony Clark, Alan Parsons

Thrillington, an orchestral version of Paul and Linda McCartney’s 1971 album Ram, had been recorded on 15-17 June 1971.

A stereo mixing session took place on 18 June. Although Paul McCartney was the producer of the sessions, he did not perform at all.

The arrangements were by Richard Hewson, who had been given free rein by the McCartneys to rework the Ram songs. Hewson was paid £100 for each song, and conducted the session musicians.

In addition to the 12 Ram songs, Hewson also arranged a version of ‘Oh Woman, Oh Why’, the b-side of Paul McCartney’s debut solo single ‘Another Day’.

The musicians:

  • Vic Flick: electric guitar, acoustic guitar
  • Herbie Flowers: bass guitar, tuba
  • Steve Gray: piano
  • Roger Coulan: organ
  • Clem Cattini: drums
  • Jim Lawless, Chris Karan: percussion
  • The Mike Sammes Singers: vocals
  • The Swingle Singers: vocals
  • Carl Dolmetsch Family: recorders
  • Unknown: strings, brass, woodwind

Thrillington was shelved for six years, and eventually released in 1977. It was credited to the pseudonymous Percy ‘Thrills’ Thrillington.
